content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (fallback target).**

Section 14.1 has a genuine insurance clause — CGL ($2M primary limits), fidelity ($10M), workers' compensation as mandated by state law, all-risk property, "A"-rated carriers, 30 days' notice of cancellation, and annual/on-request certificates. Those latter two items already satisfy the workers' comp and certificate elements of the preferred list, so I did not restate them.

The gap is substantive: no professional liability (E&O) and no cyber/privacy coverage anywhere in the document (searches returned nothing outside §14), which fails both fallback elements for a vendor processing our Items and customer data. I stayed at fallback rather than upgrading to preferred limits, and made the single shortest change — a new item 5 in the 14.1(A) schedule adding E&O at $1,000,000 and cyber/privacy at $2,000,000. Placing it inside the existing schedule means the "at its own cost and expense" lead-in and the 14.1(B) notice/certificate machinery ("coverage required by this Section") pick up the new policies with no collateral edits and no added boilerplate. The preferred-level shortfalls (E&O $2M, cyber $5M) are noted in the rationale only.
